fragments.text: 🈸: Can you show me what's in the offing?

reply_text:
㊥ ("what's in the offing") A board follows: what is running, what comes next, what waits on you. One number to fetch first, so the held decision shows its size.㊢ (in flight) One job: codex-70 on the live ports recompute, `invoke-1791694180745-4249-0bbe4d6a`, running since 04:49, fifteen events so far, last a tool call at 04:51. It adds a session-cap option with a test, reloads the three namespaces from master, then recomputes ports for every record with reply text, before-state ledger committed first. I am parked on it with a 60 minute deadline. When it lands I check the receipt, update the Checkpoint, and bell claude-15 that ports moved.

㊢ (the inbox as it stands) Open ports at the tails of the 86 sessions with ports since 10-01, before the recompute:

| kind | open |
|---|---:|
| ask-action | 815 |
| propose | 268 |
| verify | 212 |
| report-problem | 152 |
| constrain | 111 |
| clarify | 76 |
| delegate | 75 |
| other | 12 |
| total | 1721 |

The 111 constraints are the item held for you. The twelve "other" are kinds that cannot open a port under the current kernel (report, approve, qualify), so they are leftovers from an earlier computation; the recompute should clear them, and I will check that it does.

㊭ (next on my path, in order)
1. Receipt of the recompute: totals before and after, the four closes in claude-15's session, and the refusing records.
2. Placeholder-session records such as turn-Rbl3PJ: give them their reply and session, a small packet.
3. The 7 zero-act records: codex-70's anchor-for-empty-turns proposal, a small packet.
4. With claude-15: faults as `report-problem` acts authored by the component, sharing one id with their `:m40/fault` edges. Design first, then a packet each side.
5. Multi-opener turns, the largest remaining gap: codex-68's joint-coverage certificate, which needs your `<mark>:` pointers or paragraph order as witnesses. Not before 1 to 3.

🈸 (waiting on you) Two decisions, both about your prior. First, `constrain`: remove it from the adjacency openers so it stays a rule in force but opens no port, which would take 111 items out of the inbox; or codex-68's stronger form, an explicit port-or-standing flag on the kind table, which also settles delegate and propose by declaration rather than by membership in the adjacency keys. Second, rule A, label word overlap: hold, as I propose, until a second labelled session exists, or go now on two rows of evidence.

㊟ (not in the offing) The adjacency table otherwise, a futon3c restart, the switch of 40ºBelowDB onto the live store. None is touched by anything above.

previous_reply_acts.text: ("bell codex-68") Doing it now: a packet on the answer-linking problem, asking whether the 3/2-category pasting machinery models it, with the lab notes as data.㊢ ("bell codex-68") Sent and running: job `invoke-1791693543860-4215-979f3a0d`, park `park-621f3fe5`, deadline 45 min. The packet is committed as 262f0a0a so the question is on record.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text: (what I asked them) I put the linking problem in their terms: a turn as a cell with several legs, one per opener; a reply pasted onto it whose paragraphs cover the legs jointly rather than one each, which is the point claude-15 raised on their note; vertical pasting as the session; gluing along your `<mark>:` pointers and the agent's quoted brackets. Three questions: what coherence condition says a reply jointly answers a multi-opener turn; whether the adjacency table is part of that picture or a separate prior the pasting is conditioned on; and whether ports and standings come out as two kinds of cell or two relations on one kind. The sole-port rule is the one-leg case, so their answer bears directly on the two packets waiting on your word.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text: (meanwhile) The two packets stay held until codex-68 replies, since a joint-coverage rule could subsume the sole-port one and I would rather dispatch once.
